evidence: Scratch copy of the original base snapshot: `git apply --check` on judge-context/patch.diff exits 0 and checks all 8 file hunks (docs/reference/tabs.md, _layout_resolve.py, opacity.py, underline_bar.py, widgets/tabs.py, tests/renderables/test_opacity.py, tests/renderables/test_underline_bar.py, tests/test_tabs.py).
Staged diff in generated/ (git diff --cached) matches judge-context/patch.diff line-for-line once index lines are ignored, so the generated tree is the patch.
checks.json reports patch_applies=true and no commands; no tests were executed, per the experiment setup.
New Tabs/Tab module at src/textual/widgets/tabs.py, the same location as reference/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py.
UnderlineBar.clickable_ranges is added in src/textual/renderables/underline_bar.py:28, matching reference underline_bar.py:23.
Opacity fix at src/textual/renderables/opacity.py:36-44 (`style + blended` at :43) matches reference opacity.py:41.
Shared layout code stays in src/textual/_layout_resolve.py; the only change there is the Edge docstring (lines 13-22), so the resolver logic is untouched.

Tab(label, name=None) with name defaulting to label (generated/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:25-46) matches the reference @dataclass Tab (reference tabs.py:24-25) in fields, defaults, equality and repr.
Tabs.__init__ parameters, order and defaults (generated tabs.py:266-281) match reference Tabs.__init__ (reference tabs.py:199-212).

Public methods exist with matching names: activate_next_tab, activate_previous_tab, activate_tab_by_first_char, activate_tab_by_number, find_tab_by_name, action_range_clicked (generated tabs.py:364-426); reference has the same set.
UnderlineBar(highlight_range, highlight_style, background_style, clickable_ranges=None, width=None) (underline_bar.py:23-28) matches reference parameter order.

Minor internal divergence, not exported in __all__ in either version: generated TabsRenderable.__init__ (tabs.py:109-129) takes positional bar_position and no width, while reference TabsRenderable (tabs.py:48-60) is keyword-only with bar_offset and width. Tabs._bar_position (tabs.py:264) also differs from reference _bar_offset (reference tabs.py:197).
criteria.deficiency: None blocking. The TabsRenderable constructor and private reactive name differ from the reference, but neither is in __all__ or the documented API.

evidence: widgets/tabs.py:12-18 imports events, _layout_resolve, keys, reactive, renderables.opacity, renderables.underline_bar and widget, all downward into core modules, the same set as the reference.
renderables/underline_bar.py:3-5 imports only rich modules, so the renderable layer does not depend on widgets.
Relative imports (`from .. import events`, `from ..widget import Widget`) match the existing widgets/_header.py:13-15 convention.

The reference does not register Tabs in widgets/__init__.py (its __all__ list does not include Tabs), and the generated tree does not either, so there is no missing registration relative to the reference.
docs/reference/tabs.md:1 (`::: textual.widgets.tabs.Tabs`) is added, matching reference docs/reference/tabs.md.
No new third-party dependency. The code uses rich (already a declared dependency, pyproject.toml:22, rich ^11.2.0) and textual internals only.
Click metadata for inactive tabs is attached in TabsRenderable (generated tabs.py:207-209); the active tab carries none (tabs.py:200-205), matching the reference split.
UnderlineBar receives generic clickable_ranges and applies @click spans (generated underline_bar.py:94-96), the same responsibility split as reference underline_bar.py:91-94.
Widget state (active name, bar position, animation) lives in Tabs (tabs.py:263-315) and rendering in TabsRenderable (tabs.py:94-225).
Padding is resolved through the shared layout_resolve using Edge-protocol objects (_PaddingEdge at generated tabs.py:50-55; call at tabs.py:146-149), not a parallel algorithm.
Animation uses the widget animator via self.animate with duration and easing (tabs.py:306-313), matching the reference watch__ pattern.
Click dispatch uses the existing path: broker_event -> Widget.action -> app.action -> dispatch_action (app.py:621-626; widget.py:291), reaching action_range_clicked (tabs.py:426).
Not required: the reference changed Edge to a NamedTuple in _layout_resolve.py; the candidate does not, and this is not a deficiency.
Tab is pure data with no rendering or I/O (tabs.py:25-46); rendering lives in TabsRenderable (tabs.py:94-225); key handling and state live in Tabs (tabs.py:328-362).
Escape awaits the async app.set_focus (generated tabs.py:353; app.py:306 is `async def set_focus`). The reference calls it without await (reference tabs.py:248), so the candidate is correct here.
Google-style Args/Returns docstrings match the repo style (tabs.py:179-186, 297-308; underline_bar.py:9-21).
async def on_key (tabs.py:328) matches the inherited Widget.on_key signature (widget.py:356).
Tests follow the existing tests/renderables and tests/test_*.py layout and reuse the tests/utilities/render helper (tests/renderables/test_underline_bar.py:132-186, tests/test_tabs.py:1-30).
Dedup by name keeps first position and last label (generated tabs.py:76-91, _displayed_tabs), matching the reference dict-based behavior.

Active tab has no click action and inactive tabs get range_clicked meta (tabs.py:200-212). Bar interpolates over label ranges (tabs.py:171-191). Selection ranges cover whole padded spans (tabs.py:159-168).

All options are accepted and used, not just stored: tab_padding (tabs.py:146), inactive_text_opacity (tabs.py:212), animation_duration/animation_function (tabs.py:309-311), search_by_first_character (tabs.py:360), active/inactive tab and bar styles (tabs.py:198-209, 219-220).

Reference defects the candidate avoids: (1) reference tabs.py:217 `active_tab or next(iter(self.tabs), None)` stores a Tab object when active_tab is None, so the first tab is never styled active; generated tabs.py:297 uses tabs[0].name. (2) reference tabs.py:143-145 computes the selection range after the cursor reaches the span end, so "One" with padding 1 yields (4,9) instead of (0,5); generated tabs.py:165 yields the correct span. (3) Escape is unawaited in the reference (tabs.py:248).

Shared limitation, not a differentiator: activate_next_tab/activate_previous_tab walk the full tab list (generated tabs.py:364-371; reference tabs.py:260-264), so with duplicate names Right can stall on a hidden duplicate. The reference has the same logic.
criteria.deficiency: None blocking. The duplicate-name Right-key stall is shared with the reference, so it does not count against the candidate.
